correctness.rationale: The cubic graph has 36 edges, each selected matching edge edge-dominates at most five, hence every maximal matching has at least eight edges. Exhaustive independent eight-set plus complementary perfect-matching enumeration finds exactly 90 minimum maximal matchings; a separately designed C++ matched/unmatched decision tree independently obtains precisely the same canonical 90 states. Complete 4005 unordered-pair comparison yields 0, 180, 180 and 522 edges for budgets 1–4, respectively. Independent certificate checker reconstructs all graph edges, maxinality, transitions and all-source BFS distances. Three isomorphic 30-state, degree-four, radius/diameter-five components at budgets 2 and 3 follow; budget 4 is connected, radius 3 and diameter 4. Rotational/reflection automorphisms are verified explicitly. Verification uses actual included source files and complete certificate, not sampling.

value.rationale: The Nauru graph is a natural classical symmetric cubic benchmark in the edge-domination/saturation-number literature. Minimum maximal matchings are independent edge-dominating sets; analyzing the minimum set alone does not determine whether one efficient solution can transform into another without increasing resources. The complete 90-state classification exhibits a sharp change from 90 frozen optima at one edge, to three isomorphic 30-state four-regular reconfiguration regions at two and three edges, to a connected finite graph with sharp diameter four at four-edge simultaneous substitutions. This identifies a substantive optimality/mobility boundary and a symmetry-enforced obstruction, not a routine parameter increment or arbitrary slice.
